Am. 57(1), 1975, pp. 233-237, Eq. 1 and Eq. 2; ledger row fletcher-1975-flute-blowing-pressure-and-jet-length), p [mbar] = 0.008 nu [Hz] and l [mm] = 1.8 + 100 nu^(-1/2), at each tube's equal-tempered pitch: pressure 117.5 Pa and cut-up 10.05 mm at D3 to 395.1 Pa and 6.30 mm at B4. Fletcher 2005 points to the same paper (its ref 12) for the jet speed 'as in the flute', so the step from the flute to a stopped pipe is an ANALOGY, made by that source and by this recipe, not a measurement. The plotted measurements (Figs. 1 and 2) span C4 (262 Hz) to about C7; the text adds that the pressure relation also holds for one player on the alto (G) flute, whose lowest note is G3 (196 Hz), without showing data. the blowing pressure reaches the voice as a staircase at the cards' control rate, 1000 Hz: fs-scenario samples the gesture once per control tick and the voice holds that value until the next. A 50 ms onset ramp arrives as 50 steps, the first jumping from 0 to 1/50 of the target pressure, and the 10.5 ms release as about 10, the last dropping to 0. A finer rate is refused (MagentaBadger, Agent Mail 8043: 2000 and 4000 Hz on recorder a1 and whistle D5, 48000 Hz on recorder f1 and a1, whistle D5 and G5 and flute G4): a smooth ramp passes through pressures of a fraction of a Pa, where the jet is slower than its convection history allows, and the voice refuses rather than run outside its domain. A real breath passes those pressures in a few milliseconds; below some speed there is a slow viscous flow and no convected jet. The cards stay at 1000 Hz until the jet has a stated state below its lowest valid speed
column5: onset and release claims: speaking time, the attack transient and any line at 1 kHz; no finer rate renders, so the staircase's own effect on the attack cannot be A/B tested
column6: a jet with a stated state below its lowest valid speed (no jet below a stated threshold speed, or a convection history sized for the slowest jet the gesture reaches); then the cards move to a fine control rate with their controls budget raised
